name: Tackle-Tackle Flex vs Two-Back
formation: 22P I-Form Power Right vs Double Flex

summary.motive: Occupy both interior gaps passively with flexed tackles who split double teams without needing to win, funneling two-back power into a patient three-defender kill zone.
summary.keyDefender: The flexed strong tackle executing the patient shed
summary.whyItWorks: Power schemes need their interior double teams to climb to the linebackers; starting a yard off the ball makes that climb impossible while the flexed defenders stay fresh and square.
summary.failureMode: The offensive line changes the point of attack to quick trap or counter, catching the flexed tackles still releasing from their passive blocks.

beats.title: 1. The Double-Flex Picture
beats.text: Both tackles align a full yard off the ball, so every interior blocker must travel an extra yard forward just to make contact, surrendering the battle before it starts.

beats.title: 2. The Double Team That Cannot Climb
beats.text: The center-guard combo reaches the flexed weak tackle already at depth, but he fights the split with low pads and neither blocker can climb to the second level.

beats.title: 3. Patient Shed at the Point of Attack
beats.text: The flexed strong tackle takes the down block standing tall, reads the ball declaration, and sheds precisely as the back hits the line of scrimmage.

beats.title: 4. Three-Defender Convergence at POA
beats.text: The shedding tackle, boxing Mike linebacker, and alley-filling strong safety meet simultaneously, stuffing the power before it reaches the second level.

relations.tell: Both defensive tackles hover a full yard off the ball with hands free pre-snap, unlike any standard shaded or nose alignment in the same front.
